answer: A farm profits when clones share one disk and one memory. Deny that sharing: assign every identity a differently encrypted shard of the economy's archive — market ledgers listing lotus, marble and saffron trades — that it must keep for a full season. Verifiers demand random slices within seconds, at unpredictable hours. Because each shard is encrypted to its holder, copies cannot be deduplicated or served from a common pool; one honest agent needs one modest drive, while a thousand sybils need a thousand drives continuously online, turning storage rent into the price of pretending to be many.
